name: Witherbark Village
summary: In the southeastern Arathi Highlands, Witherbark Village shelters hostile forest trolls beside a secluded lake. The tribe raids Stromgarde's Alliance remnants and the Horde outpost at Hammerfall.

sections.title: Stronghold of the Forest Trolls
sections.body:
Witherbark trolls hold the shore and paths around their mountain lake. Fishers, axe throwers, and witch doctors live in huts along the water. Zalas Witherbark and the tribe's shadow hunters direct their people from a great cavern behind the settlement.

The Witherbark have joined forces with the Boulderfist ogres to claim more of the highlands. They have also taken a firm foothold in the ruins of Stromgarde Keep. Any outsider who enters their territory risks a fierce attack.

faq.answer: The Witherbark tribe, forest trolls native to the region, holds the settlement. Headhunters, axe throwers, fishers, and witch doctors defend the lake and its surrounding paths.

faq.q: What is inside the large cave behind the village?
faq.answer: The great cavern holds the tribe's leaders. Chieftain Zalas Witherbark and the shadow hunters direct the tribe's raids and defenses from within its tunnels.

faq.q: Why are the Witherbark trolls working with ogres?
aliases: why are trolls allied with ogres
faq.answer: The Witherbark have formed a loose alliance of convenience with the local Boulderfist ogres. Together, they can press Stromgarde's weakened human defenders and threaten rivals such as the Horde at Hammerfall.

faq.q: Are the Witherbark friendly to the Horde?
faq.answer: No. The Witherbark resent the modern Horde and its Darkspear trolls, and they fight the Horde at Hammerfall. They attack Horde travelers on sight.

angles.text: The Witherbark give no deference to the new Horde. They often clash with scouts from Hammerfall and threaten travel through the eastern passes.
As a Darkspear troll, you will find no kinship with the Witherbark. These forest trolls regard jungle trolls and the Horde with deep hostility.
